translations.text: The bride says:
Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth, for your breasts are better than wine.
And the fragrance of your oils is better than all incense. Your name is fragrant oil poured out; therefore the maidens loved you.

And they drew you; we will run after the fragrance of your oils. The bride tells the maidens about the bridegroom and what he bestowed on her: The king brought me into his chamber. After the bride has told the maidens, they say: We will rejoice and be glad in you, and we will love your breasts more than wine. The maidens speak to the bride in the bridegroom’s name: Uprightness loved you.
The bride says: I am black and beautiful, daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar and like Solomon’s pavilion.
Do not look at me because I have become black and dark, for the sun looked harshly upon me. My mother’s sons fought against me and made me keeper of the vineyards, for I did not keep my own vineyard.

The bride says to the bridegroom: Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where do you pasture your flock? Where do you let it rest at noon? Otherwise I may become like an outcast among the flocks of your companions.
The bridegroom says to the bride: If you do not know yourself, beautiful one among women, go out following the tracks of the flocks, and pasture your young goats beside the shepherds’ tents.
I have compared you, my companion, to my horses in Pharaoh’s chariots.
The maidens say to the bride: For your cheeks have become beautiful, like a turtledove’s, and your neck like necklaces.
We will make you ornaments of gold with studs of silver,
until the king receives you into his embrace. The bride says to herself and to the bridegroom: My nard gave forth its fragrance.
My beloved is a bundle of myrrh to me; he will rest between my breasts.
My beloved is a cluster of henna to me among the vineyards of En-gedi.
The bridegroom says to the bride: Behold, you are beautiful, my companion; behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are doves.
The bride says to the bridegroom: Look, you are handsome, my beloved, and beautiful too, beside our shaded couch.
The beams of our houses are cedars; our ceiling panels are cypresses.
The bridegroom says to himself and to the bride:
I am a flower of the fields, a lily of the valleys.
Like a lily among thorns, so is my companion among the daughters.
The bride says to the bridegroom: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest, so is my beloved among the sons. I longed to sit in his shade, and I sat there, and his fruit is sweet to my taste.
The bride says to the maidens: Bring me into the house of wine; set love over me.
Strengthen me with oil; heap apples upon me, for I am faint with love.
His left hand is beneath my head, and his right hand will embrace me.
The bride says to the maidens: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and the mighty forces of the field, not to stir up or awaken love until it wishes.
She heard the bridegroom’s voice and says: The voice of my beloved! Look, he has come, running over the mountains, leaping over the hills.

My beloved is like a gazelle or a young deer upon the mountains of Bethel. The bride points out the bridegroom to the maidens and says: Look, he stands beyond our wall, peering through the windows, looking through the lattice.
My beloved answers me and says: Rise, come, my companion, my beautiful one, my dove.
For behold, winter has passed; the rains have passed and gone away.
The flowers have appeared in our land; the time for pruning has come; the voice of the turtledove has been heard in our land.
The fig tree has put out its buds; our flowering vines have given off their fragrance. Arise, come, my companion, my beautiful one, my dove, and come away.
My little dove, under the shelter of your rock, beside the buttress of your wall, show me your face and let me hear your voice, for your voice is sweet and your appearance beautiful.
The bridegroom says this to the maidens: Catch for us the little foxes that ruin the vineyards, for our vineyards are in bloom.
The bride says this: My beloved is mine, and I am his; he grazes among the lilies.
Until the day grows light and the shadows move away, turn back, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young deer on the incense-bearing mountains.
On my bed at night I sought the one my soul loved. I sought him and did not find him; I called, but he did not answer me.
I will rise and go around the city, through the streets and the squares, and seek the one my soul loved. I sought him and did not find him; I called him, but he did not answer me.
The watchmen who went around the city found me. The bride says to the watchmen: Have you seen the one my soul loved?

When I had passed a little beyond them, I found the one whom my soul loved. Having found the bridegroom, she says: I held him and did not let him go until I brought him into my mother’s house and into the chamber of the one who conceived me.
The bride puts the maidens under oath a second time: I put you under oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and the strengths of the field: do not rouse or awaken love until it wishes.
The bridegroom says of the bride: Who is this coming up from the wilderness like smoke rising in a column, sending up myrrh and frankincense, with every fragrant powder of the perfume makers?
The maidens said this: Look, Solomon's couch! Sixty armed men surround it, from among the mighty men of Israel.
All of them carry swords and are skilled in war, each man with his sword at his thigh because of the terrors of the night.
King Solomon made himself a palanquin from the wood of Lebanon.
He made its pillars of silver, its base of gold, and its canopy of purple; its interior was set with jewels, spread with love from the daughters of Jerusalem.
Go out, daughters of Zion, and look at King Solomon wearing the crown with which his mother crowned him on his wedding day, on the day of his heart's joy.
The bridegroom says to the bride:
Look, you are beautiful, my companion; look, you are beautiful. Your eyes are doves, apart from your silence. Your hair is like flocks of goats that have appeared from Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of shorn sheep coming up from washing. All of them bear twins, and none among them is childless.
Your lips are like a scarlet thread, and your words are beautiful. Your cheeks are like the rind of a pomegranate, apart from your silence.
Your neck is like David’s tower, which is built in Talpioth. A thousand shields hang from it, and all the arrows of armed warriors.
Your two breasts are like two young gazelles, twins, grazing among the lilies.
Until the day fades and the shadows move away, I will go to the mountain of myrrh and the hill of frankincense.
You are altogether beautiful, my companion, and there is no blemish in you.
Come from Lebanon, bride; come here from Lebanon. Come and pass from the summit of faith, from the peak of Senir and Hermon, from the lions' thickets and the mountains of leopards.
You have captivated our hearts, our sister, bride; you have captivated our hearts with one of your eyes and with one four-stranded necklace on your neck.
How beautiful are your breasts, my sister, my bride! How much more beautiful are your breasts than wine, and the fragrance of your garments than all spices!
Your lips drip honey, my sister, my bride; honey and milk are under your tongue, and the fragrance of your garments is like the fragrance of frankincense.
My sister, my bride, is a locked garden, a locked garden and a sealed spring.
Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranate trees with fruit-bearing trees, henna with nard,
nard and saffron, aromatic cane and cinnamon, with all the trees of Lebanon, myrrh and aloes, with all the finest spices.
A fountain of gardens and a spring of living water flowing from Lebanon.

Rise, north wind, and come, south wind! Blow upon my garden, and let my spices spread their fragrance.
The bride asks her bridegroom to come down.
Let my beloved come down into his garden and eat the fruit of his trees.
The bridegroom speaks to the bride.
I entered my garden, my sister, my bride; I gathered my myrrh with my spices, ate my bread with my honey, and drank my wine with my milk. Eat, my friends, and drink; become drunk, my beloved ones!

I sleep, but my heart is awake.
The bride hears the bridegroom knocking at the door.
The voice of my beloved! He knocks at the door.
The bridegroom says:
Open to me, my sister, my companion, my dove, my perfect one, for my head is covered with dew, and my locks with the moisture of the night.

The bride says this:
I have taken off my tunic; how can I put it on? I have washed my feet; how can I soil them?
My nephew stretched his hand through the window, and my belly was stirred for him.
I rose to open to my beloved. My hands dripped myrrh, and my fingers abundant myrrh upon the handles of the bolt.
I opened to my beloved, but my beloved had passed on, and my soul went out at his words. I sought him but did not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.
The watchmen who went around the city found me; they struck and wounded me. The watchmen of the walls took my cloak from me.
I put you under oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and strengths of the field: if you find my beloved, tell him that I am consumed with longing for your love.

The daughters of Jerusalem and the guards of the walls ask the bride: What is your nephew compared with other nephews, you who are beautiful among women? What is your nephew compared with other nephews, that you have adjured us so?

The bride describes her beloved, what sort of man he was.
My beloved is white and ruddy, chosen from among tens of thousands.
His head is of fine gold; his locks are curled, black as a raven.
His eyes are like doves beside abundant waters, washed in milk, sitting beside overflowing waters.
His cheeks are like beds of spices, giving off the sweet fragrance of perfumers. His lips are lilies, flowing with abundant myrrh.
His hands are turned gold, set with stones of Tarshish. His belly is an ivory panel, inlaid with sapphire stones.
His legs are marble pillars set upon golden bases. His appearance is like the choicest fir trees of Lebanon.
His throat is full of sweetness, and he is altogether desirable. This is my beloved, and this is my companion, daughters of Jerusalem.

The daughters of Jerusalem ask where her beloved has gone—that is, the bride’s beloved.
Where has your beloved gone, you beautiful one among women? Which way has your beloved turned, so that we too may seek him with you?
The bride answers and says:
My beloved went down into his garden, to the beds of spices, to tend his flock in the gardens and gather lilies.
I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine, he who tends his flock among the lilies.
The bridegroom says to the bride: You are lovely, my companion, like delight, beautiful as Jerusalem, awesomely arrayed.
Turn your eyes away from me, for they have intoxicated me. Your hair is like flocks of goats that appeared from Gilead.
Your teeth are like flocks of shorn sheep coming up from washing. All of them bear twins, and none among them is barren.
Your lips are like a scarlet thread, and your words are beautiful. Your cheeks are like the rind of a pomegranate, apart from your silence.
There are sixty queens and eighty concubines, and young women beyond number.
My dove, my perfect one, is unique. She is her mother's only one, the chosen one of her who bore her. The daughters saw her and called her blessed; the queens and concubines praised her.
The daughters and queens saw the bride and called her blessed: Who is this who appears like the dawn, beautiful as the moon, excellent as the sun, awesomely arrayed?

The bridegroom says to the bride: I went down to the walnut gardens to look at the produce of the watercourses, to see whether the vine had blossomed, whether the cypress had blossomed, whether the pomegranate trees had blossomed.
The bride says to the bridegroom: There I will give you my breasts. My soul did not know; it made me like the chariots of Amminadab.

The daughters and queens say to the bride: Return, Shunammite, return, return, so that we may look at you. The bridegroom says this to the daughters and queens: What do you see in the Shunammite, who comes advancing like companies of armies?
For your steps have become beautiful in sandals, daughter of Nadab. The shape of your thighs is like cast beads, the work of a skilled craftsman.
Your navel is a turned bowl, never lacking mixed wine. Your belly is like a heap of wheat surrounded by lilies.
Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.
Your neck is like an ivory tower. Your eyes are like the pool of Heshbon at the gates of many daughters. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon that looks toward Damascus.
Your head upon you is like Carmel. The braids of your hair are like purple, like a king with a crown on his head in the racecourses.
How beautiful you have become, and how sweet you have become, O love, in your delight!
Your stature resembles a palm tree, and your breasts resemble clusters of grapes.
I said: I will climb the palm tree and take hold of its heights. Let your breasts be like clusters of grapes on a vine, and the scent of your nose like apples.
Your throat is like fine wine. The bride speaks on behalf of the daughters and queens: Going straight after my nephew, satisfying my lips and teeth.
I belong to my nephew, and he turns toward me.
Come, my nephew, let us go out into the fields. Let us spend the night in the villages and gardens; let us go early to the vineyards.
Let us see whether the vine has blossomed, whether the cypress has blossomed, whether the pomegranate tree has blossomed. There I will give you my breasts.
The mandrakes have given off their fragrance, and at our doors are all kinds of fruits, the new along with the old, which my mother gave me. I have kept them for you, my nephew.
If only you, my nephew, had nursed at my mother’s breasts! Finding you outside, I would kiss you, and you would not despise me.
I will take you and bring you into my mother's house and into the chamber of her who conceived me. I will give you wine from the oil makers to drink, and syrup from my pomegranates.
His left hand is under my head, and his right hand will embrace me.
I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and strengths of the field: do not rouse or awaken love until it wishes.

The daughters and queens say: Who is this coming up, whitened, leaning on her nephew? The bridegroom says to the bride: Under the apple tree I awakened you. There your mother was in labor with you; there she who bore you was in labor.
Set me as a seal upon your heart and as a signet ring upon your arm, for love is strong as death, and jealousy is fierce as hell. Its flashes are like flashes of blazing fire.
Many waters cannot quench love, and rivers cannot hold it back. If a man gave all his possessions for love, he would be utterly despised.
Our sister is little, and she has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister on the day when she is spoken to?
If she is a wall, we will build silver battlements upon her. If she is a door, we will fit her with fir-wood boards.
The bride speaks boldly and says: I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers. In his eyes I was like one who finds peace.
Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon. He entrusted his vineyard to keepers. Each man was to bring a thousand pieces of silver for its fruit.
My vineyard is mine, before me. The thousand pieces belong to Solomon, and two hundred to the keepers who guard its fruit.
The bride says: You who dwell in the gardens, others listen to you. Let me hear your voice.
Flee, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young deer upon the mountains that bear spices. The maidens and the queens say:
I knew that the body brings joy to youth. May our king lift it up into his storehouses. Upon our thrones, like a golden palm, may our bowls be filled with fragrant ointment.
May the king return again to youth.
The beloved is in our chambers; let us sing of love.
The bridegroom says: I myself am at the psaltery. I will sing with my companions. Let us sing and be glad.
The bride, the daughters, and the maidens say: Beloved king, although we have hidden our eyes from the vision, [?] fifty-year-olds.

The Lord made you, established you, and prepared you from the womb, you who are beautiful among women. Your mother will bear an unblemished body. On the same passage, from another recension, for it read as follows.
